leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B001 prize to Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov, so the laureate set is identical and Lotte Bjerre Knudsen is omitted by all six. Shared: the physiology-to-therapy chain (human incretin physiology, identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, GLP-1/GLP-2 biology), independent confirmation, and large randomized outcome trials. Citations differ in wording only: all six anchor on GLP-1 physiology and the identity or active form of the peptide, and the enabled therapies are described as incretin-based treatment of diabetes and obesity (type 2 diabetes explicitly in four). Not shared: how much weight to give the omission of Knudsen, and how settled the early peptide-identification priority is. Several members state that unanimity is not itself the argument.

areas_of_agreement: All six members put the same three names (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov) on B001 as a single-achievement prize and frame the citation around physiology and identification of the active peptide, not around a particular drug.
All six describe B001 as mature, with decades of independent confirmation and randomized outcome evidence in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints.

All six name attribution as the strongest reservation: contested early peptide-identification priority (Habener and others are not among the credited names) and the omission of Knudsen under the three-person limit.

All six list B045 (CAR-T) as an alternative; four (El-Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson) list B004 (BCR-ABL inhibition) and two (Linnarsson, Wahren-Herlenius) list B043 (unfolded protein response) as the other alternative.

Several members say the Knudsen omission is a real cost and should be made explicitly as a judgement, not described as free or as a finding that development work is lesser (El-Manira, Sandberg, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius, Svenningsson).
Members who comment on B043 describe Mori and Walter as the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, with clinical translation still emerging; none proposes it ahead of B001 this year.
Members who comment on optogenetics (B039) see a six-name credit problem against a three-person cap and treat it as a tool whose medical case rests on enabling impact.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus development: whether Knudsen's long-acting analogue chemistry extends an already-established mechanism (Svenningsson's reading) or is the step that converted the physiology into the therapy the citation celebrates (raised by El-Manira, Linnarsson and Perlmann as a cost). The configurations do not differ on this, but the reasoning does.

Weight of therapeutic maturity versus conceptual novelty among alternatives: B045 is favoured by some as a new modality, while B004 is described as an optimization of an established kinase-targeting paradigm and, by Perlmann and Linnarsson, with a drug-framed prize reading as a medicinal-chemistry award (Linnarsson ranked it lower than Perlmann did).

How much weight a basic-mechanism discovery with emerging clinical translation (B043) should carry relative to demonstrated outcome benefit; Wahren-Herlenius, Linnarsson and Svenningsson describe it as a later or second-prize candidate, while Sandberg says limited translation does not disqualify it.

Whether the prior recognition of B004 (Lasker) and of apoptosis in 2002 (relevant to B003) should lower a candidate's standing: Perlmann says a Lasker award is not a Nobel criterion, whereas other members cite it as late confirmation of an established paradigm.
Whether a tool (B039) deserves the same priority as a discovery that changed treatment; members describe this as a judgement call.
attribution_disputes: B001: priority for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide between Mojsov and the Habener group (not among credited names) is not settled by the supplied evidence; Wahren-Herlenius says it is the one point that could change her view of the trio. Several members state they rely on recollection of the chronology.

B001: Knudsen is omitted by all six configurations; Svenningsson would keep her out while recording that her case deserves a hearing under a drug-development framing, and El-Manira and Sandberg say a swap of one of the three would be the only alternative.

B045 (CAR-T): the credited names are June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, but the original chimeric receptor concept (Eshhar, Gross) is not credited. Svenningsson and Linnarsson would narrow to June and Sadelain and exclude Rosenberg (Linnarsson stated this explicitly); Sandberg and Linnarsson regard the Eshhar gap as more serious than the B001 priority question.

B004: upstream BCR-ABL biology (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) lies outside the credited trio of Druker, Sawyers and Lydon, and the industry-academic split in the compound programme complicates who discovered what.

B039: six credited names (Boyden, Bamberg, Nagel, Miesenbock, Deisseroth, Hegemann) against a three-person cap; Sandberg's proposed trio of Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann is contested by members who see no non-arbitrary split.

B003: Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer are not among the credited names, and Vaux's survival work and the Cory-Adams translocation work are distinct contributions, so no tidy three-person allocation has been shown among four credited names.

Members' round-1 statements describe each other's opening rankings inconsistently in places (for example, which of B012, B014 and B043 sit where); only the six preferred configurations and listed alternatives are counted here.
maturity_disputes: B001 is described by all six as mature; Linnarsson, Perlmann, El-Manira and Sandberg add that recognition is timely or overdue. Long-term safety of chronic use is still being characterized (El-Manira, Linnarsson) but is not treated as bearing on the core discovery.
B043: clinical and physiological consequences are still emerging (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Wahren-Herlenius, Svenningsson), against thirty years of confirmation of the mechanism.
B039: clinical use of optogenetics is still nascent (El-Manira, Sandberg).
B042 (cGAS-STING): mechanism is clear, but pathway modulation has not yet shown clinical benefit (Perlmann, citing Sandberg's own reservation).
B040 (SMN2 splicing and nusinersen): described by Perlmann as a mechanistically clear success in a newer field, with the SMN1 gene discovery outside the credited names.
B004: maturity is not disputed, but the question is whether it reads as late confirmation of an established paradigm.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: El-Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons, unrelated to any shortlisted ballot.
Perlmann discloses past co-authorship with Svenningsson and, once, El-Manira, and does not regard it as a conflict.
Svenningsson (chair) discloses work with Paul Greengard (not a candidate) and co-authorship with Perlmann, which does not bear on any shortlisted name; no shared-institution tie assumed.
Linnarsson discloses co-authorship with Sandberg on a spatial-transcriptomics paper; no credited name on any shortlisted ballot is involved.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen and a shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation; none of the shortlisted candidates is documented as connected.
No member reports a conflict with any credited name on the shortlist, and none requests recusal.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee examine primary evidence for identification of the active GLP-1 peptide, rather than recollection, to decide whether Mojsov's credit relative to the Habener group supports her place in the trio?
Is a three-name B001 prize without Knudsen acceptable, and if not, which one of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov would be replaced and on what documented ground?
Should the B001 citation be worded to name physiology and the identity or active form of the peptide only, and should it mention type 2 diabetes alone or diabetes and obesity?
If B045 is the lead alternative, is a June and Sadelain core without Eshhar and Gross acceptable, and is Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy work a distinct achievement or part of the same claim?
Given the three-person cap, does any member advocate a two-part configuration that pairs B001 with B045, B043 or B004, and if so which names would be dropped from B001?

Is B004 held back chiefly by the upstream BCR-ABL credit (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore), by the Lasker recognition, or by its drug-development framing, and can the committee agree which of these is a valid ground?
Does anyone wish to move B003 (BCL-2) or B043 higher once attribution is examined (Svenningsson stated this for both), and what tidy allocation would they propose?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a unanimous single-part B001 configuration with an identical laureate trio, with the debate concentrated in attribution (the omission of Knudsen and the unsettled early peptide-identification priority) and in how alternatives would be handled if B001 stalled. Alternatives are B045 (listed by all six), B004 (four members) and B043 (two members). No member has proposed a second prize part, and no conflicts relating to credited names were disclosed. Round 2 should settle the evidence behind the contested credit and the citation wording before any alternative is considered.
